title: Time-Resolved Magnetic Imaging with Ultrafast Electron Pulser: Spin-Wave Generation in Topological Spin Textures
content: In recent years, spin waves (or magnons) have garnered significant attention due to their critical role in elucidating fundamental physics phenomena in solid-state systems and their promising applications in future low-energy devices, such as those used for information communications and neuromorphic computing. However, probing spin-wave behavior in complex spin textures and nano-devices remains challenging for three main reasons. First, the magnon energies typically range from µeV to meV scale—a very small energy level that demands extremely sensitive experimental techniques. Second, the propagation distance of spin waves is limited by factors such as Gilbert damping and the scattering of magnons by local magnetic domain structures. Even in low damping materials like YIG or Permalloy, spin waves quickly lose amplitude over just a few microns, necessitating high spatial resolution to resolve their details. Third, practical spin-wave applications often operate at high frequencies (typically in the GHz range or above), which results in both shorter wavelengths and faster dynamics. Therefore, techniques with temporal resolutions on the order of nanoseconds or even picoseconds are required to capture these rapid phenomena accurately.
